title: Uniform oracle fixed points

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; section 15.1, Exercise 15.3, pp.63–64; the common numerical driver and parameterized and partial-family forms are expanded explicitly

summary: Construct one primitive-recursive self-reference compiler whose fixed-point identities hold under every oracle.
abstract: A program can act on its own index even when its running computation asks questions of an arbitrary set. The difficulty is choosing the same numerical program before that set is supplied. We construct a single ordinary primitive-recursive compiler that gives a common oracle program its own index and an external parameter. Its evaluation identity preserves both outputs and divergence for every oracle. Any ordinary total computable transformation of indices then has one primitive-recursive selector of semantic fixed points valid under all oracles, even when the transformation itself is not primitive recursive. A supplied common program also gives the corresponding result for families of partial computations. The construction separates an ordinary calculation of program text from the oracle questions asked when that text is run.
